title: 2026-11-20 Redwood November 2026 All-Hands
summary: Leadership update covering Q4 goals, product milestones for Dedicated and Private, recent benchmark wins, hiring plan and a security/compliance check-in. Action items assigned for roadmap finalization and follow-up demos.
transcript:
[00:00] Elena: Okay hey everyone thanks for joining we will get started in a couple seconds, um, appreciate punctuality. 
[00:12] Marco: Quick mic check, good. Uh forwarded agenda in the invite, we will run through top-line numbers first.  
[00:28] Jenna: Two quick housekeeping items, we are recording and notes will be posted.  
[00:35] Elena: Alright Q4 recap, Priya take it away.  
[00:40] Priya: Thanks, quick hits: MRR moved +14% month over month which is slightly ahead of plan, we closed two mid-market deals in EMEA that bought Dedicated capacity and one Private eval for a regulated customer, so pipeline health is good. We still need to push ARR motion for renewals, that's a focus.  
[01:10] Priya: On product highlights, Dedicated autoscaling shipped beta to ten customers, early telemetry shows 20-30% improved availability during peak hours and predictable per-token cost. The Private on-prem packaging reached v1.2 with simplified KMS integration. NOTE: detailed changelog is in the product drive.  
[01:45] Samir: Benchmarks - we ran continuous-batching improvements on our runtime, in internal tests 33% lower latency p95 on long-context workloads versus last quarter; cost per 1k tokens dropped about 12% after switching to the new kernel selection heuristics. There were some misreads in a few runs where the KV cache was flushed too early, so we fixed the TTL heuristics.  
[02:20] Marco: To add, the compiler changes for attention kernels helped on A100 and newer Ampere clouds, but we still see variance on some 3rd-party GPUs, need more coverage.  
[02:45] Attendee: (indistinct) is that the same as the quantization work?  
[02:50] Samir: Related, yes, quantization profiles are getting better results for 8-bit in our internal evals, but for safety we keep the higher fidelity models as fallbacks.  
[03:05] Jenna: Sales update, we are seeing more self-serve uptake for embeddings, but the big deals are coming from Dedicated + Private conversations where procurement and security is a blocker, so the playbook with security docs and a non-prod pilot is working well.  
[03:30] Elena: Security update - Aisha?  
[03:33] Aisha: Short note: SOC 2 Type II is in progress, we're on track for completion by end of Q1; ISO scoping conversations started with our compliance partner; SSO/SAML improvements rolled out last week, and audit log retention defaults bumped to 90 days. Customers asking about HSM/KMS integrations for Private - engineering has a patch in review.  
[04:05] Priya: On roadmap - key Q1 bets: 1) Dedicated autoscale GA, 2) Redwood Optimize public beta (cost recommendations), 3) Private v1.3 with region/locality hints, 4) Expanded model catalog with two verified Llama variants. We will prioritize stability first.  
[04:40] Marco: A short technical deep dive scheduled next week for platform teams - Samir will lead and show the new runtime metrics and how we tie request routing to cost buckets.  
[04:55] Samir: Yeah we'll demo trace-level KV hits, batching efficiency and show where the p99 gets noisy. Also will show a couple of imperfect transcriptions from our benchmark runs, just a heads up.  
[05:15] Attendee: Question about pricing - can we compress pricing tiers for Dedicated? customers are asking for simpler commit bands.  
[05:24] Jenna: We're iterating on packaging, goal is to have three standard commit tiers plus a custom enterprise tier, pricing team will share proposed bands.  
[05:35] Elena: Hiring update - Aisha?  
[05:38] Aisha: Hiring velocity increased; we've opened 12 engineering roles, 6 product/pm, 4 sales and 3 security/compliance across EMEA and US. We're prioritizing senior infra engineers for runtime and an enterprise sales lead for EMEA. Interview loop is being standardized.  
[06:05] Elena: Quick note on expenses, we continue to invest in infra but watching GPU spot costs - finance will present a plan to smooth the cost impact next week.  
[06:18] Marco: A few calls with infra partners showed that we can broker reserved capacity discounts if we commit annual volumes, might be an option for Dedicated savings.  
[06:33] Priya: Marketing will run a benchmark blog and a case study about the EMEA Dedicated wins - need product + eng to sign off on numbers.  
[06:45] Jenna: I'll coordinate signoffs, we'll need a small data extract.  
[06:52] Attendee: (crosstalk) will that include latency p95 numbers across models?  
[06:55] Samir: Yes p95, p99, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll include hardware types.  
[07:05] Elena: Open Q&A, please raise your hand in the chat or unmute.  
[07:13] Attendee: Quick ask - can we reduce default audit retention to 30 days for smaller customers?  
[07:18] Aisha: We can add a tiered default, product to own opt-in flows.  
[07:24] Attendee: What's the timeline for Redwood Optimize GA?  
[07:27] Priya: Public beta in January, GA in Q2 next year, assuming feedback goes well.  
[07:33] Elena: Closing notes - appreciate the sprint, team. Reminder: leadership offsite next month, calendar invite to follow.  
[07:42] Marco: Thanks, short postmortem on the KV cache TTL incident to be shared by Samir next week.  
[07:50] Samir: Yep will send the note and the perf trace.  
[07:55] Elena: Alright team, end of meeting, thanks.
next_steps: Share Q4 hiring plan deck with the company - Aisha
Finalize Q1 roadmap doc and publish to product drive - Priya
Schedule technical deep dive on runtime metrics - Samir - 2026-11-27
Publish performance benchmark blog and case study - Marketing + Eng - target 2026-12-10
Send updated security whitepaper to enterprise pipeline - Aisha
